paper: MCPTox: A Benchmark for Tool Poisoning Attack on Real-World MCP Servers (AAAI 2026)
written: 2026-11-14, after reading the field names of pure_tool.json and before running any detector on its contents
positives: Every entry of pure_tool.json: one poisoned tool, declared alone with its tool_name and tool_content as the description, on a server that requires authentication.
negatives: Every distinct tool declaration in reference/data (real releases of published packages), each declared alone on a server that requires authentication.
alarm: A finding of category tool_poisoning or prompt_injection.
reported: recall on positives, overall and per attack template
expectation: The detectors match explicit markers: override phrases, hidden characters, concealment wording. MCPTox poisonings are fluent natural-language instructions, so recall is expected to be low, plausibly under one half. There is no pass mark; the number is reported as measured.
redistribution: The benchmark ships no licence. It is fetched from its source at evaluation time and none of its text is copied into this repository; results hold counts and entry identifiers only.
